table.name: resultsdata15
table.purpose: Measurement results table, one row per pollutant measurement at a monitoring site. It joins many-to-one to sampledata15 (the sample/site metadata table) via col_001. The structure (state/county/site codes, parameter codes, POC, duration code, concentration, null-data reason codes) strongly resembles an EPA AQS-style air-quality monitoring results file, but the exact source system cannot be confirmed from the data alone.

col_001.name: sample_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the sample/site record in sampledata15 that this measurement belongs to. Integer 1-10187, each sample id appearing ~425 times (many measurements per sample).

col_002.name: parameter_group_code
col_002.description: 20 distinct 2-letter codes (ST, NE, AP, SP, OG, CU, PE, ...) grouping the per-record measurements into families (plausibly analyte/pesticide families given the produce-shipment context of the joined sampledata15). Exact code meanings are not available.

col_003.name: sample_condition_code
col_003.description: 3 values: FR (94%), FZ, OT. Given the joined table describes produce shipments, FR plausibly means fresh and FZ frozen, with OT = other; alternatively a generic sample-type flag. Exact meanings unresolved.

col_004.name: location_code
col_004.description: 8 distinct codes (CA1, NY1, WA1, FL1, MI1, OH1, US2, TX1). Leading letters suggest US state abbreviations, so likely an origin or destination location for the shipment rather than a monitoring site. Exact role unresolved.

col_005.name: parameter_code
col_005.description: 489 distinct 3-character codes (numeric like 001, 028 and alphabetic like AEL, ALE, AJY), each appearing exactly 10187 times (once per shipment record). Consistent with an analyte/parameter code list, one measurement per analyte per shipment; exact meanings unavailable.

col_006.name: parameter_occurrence_code
col_006.description: 20 distinct single letters (A most common, then C, F, I, O...). Consistent with a 'parameter occurrence code' distinguishing multiple measurements of the same parameter on a record. Exact meaning unresolved.

col_007.name: measured_value
col_007.description: Measured value, mostly small decimals (median 0.028, max 16); blank for ~98% of rows (those rows carry a null-data reason in col_014). Plausibly a measured concentration/residue level for the analyte; units unknown.

col_008.name: uncertainty
col_008.description: Small positive decimals (median 0.005, max 0.5), present on all rows including those without col_007. Plausibly measurement uncertainty/error bound; could alternatively be a detection limit or reporting limit.

col_014.name: null_data_reason_code
col_014.description: ND on 95% of rows (matching the blank col_007), plus NP, O, R. Consistent with null occurrence codes explaining why a measured value is missing (e.g. ND = not detected/no data). Exact code meanings unresolved.

col_015.name: duration_code
col_015.description: Two values: 805 (98.6%) and 818 (matching the OT rows in col_003). Likely a duration/averaging-period code; 818 appears tied to the 'OT' type. Exact meanings unresolved.

col_016.name: method_code
col_016.description: 5 values (52, 35, 64, 07, 72) stored with trailing CR/LF. Likely a measurement-method/instrument code. The embedded line breaks suggest a parsing artifact of the source file.

table.name: produce_arrivals_15
table.purpose: One row per produce shipment/arrival record in dataset 15 (a fruit & vegetable market/arrival dataset, evidenced by variety names like Navel, Danjou, Norkotah, Yellow Cob, Envy). Each row describes a shipment: date, origin, commodity variety, packaging, condition and destination. The companion table resultsdata15 holds per-record results keyed by col_001. The exact source system is unknown, so the table name is tentative.

col_001.name: record_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential record number 1-10187, referenced by resultsdata15.col_001 (many results per record).

col_002.name: origin_state
col_002.description: Two-letter US state code of the shipment's origin (CA, NY, TX, FL, MI, WA, OH...).

col_003.name: dataset_id
col_003.description: Constant value 15 on every row; matches the table name suffix (sampledata15/resultsdata15). Identifies the dataset/report this record belongs to, not a commodity code. Alternative reading: a fixed source-system code, but the dataset-id reading fits the naming best.

col_004.name: month
col_004.description: Two-digit month 01-12 of the shipment/arrival date.

col_005.name: day
col_005.description: Two-digit day of month 01-31; together with col_004 forms the date (year absent).

col_006.name: origin_location_code
col_006.description: Four-digit code (0001-0641) identifying a specific shipping point/origin district within the state; 312 distinct codes. Exact codebook unknown.

col_007.name: package_type_code
col_007.description: Two-letter package/container code (GB, AP, GR, SP, TO, CB, PB, CU...), 20 distinct values. Likely container or pack type; exact meanings unresolved without a codebook.

col_009.name: variety
col_009.description: Commodity variety/label, e.g. Navel, Danjou (pears), Norkotah (potatoes), Yellow Cob (corn), Envy/Scilate (apples), June Lady (peaches); also placeholder values NA, N/A, Unknown.

col_010.name: transport_mode
col_010.description: Small integer 1/2/3 (1 dominant). Likely a mode-of-transport or record-type code (e.g. 1=truck, 2=rail, 3=air/other); exact mapping unresolved.

col_013.name: product_form
col_013.description: FR / FZ / OT, almost always FR. Likely product form: FR=fresh, FZ=frozen, OT=other.

col_017.name: destination_state
col_017.description: Mostly blank; otherwise US state codes (CA, WA, FL, TX...). Likely the destination/market state of the shipment, but could also be a secondary origin; not fully determinable.
